title: Integration by Parts
quickIdea: Trade one integral for another using the product rule backwards: the integral of u dv is u v minus the integral of v du, and the choice of u decides whether the trade helps.
remember: Formula: the integral of u dv = u v - the integral of v du. It comes straight from integrating the product rule.
For a definite integral evaluate the product at the two limits and subtract the second integral: the integral from a to b of u dv = [u v] from a to b minus the integral from a to b of v du.
Choose u by LIATE - logarithmic, inverse trigonometric, algebraic, trigonometric, exponential - taking whichever appears first in that list as u.
A polynomial times a trigonometric or exponential factor needs as many rounds as the polynomial's degree; each round lowers the degree by one. x^2 cos x needs two rounds.
A polynomial times a logarithm or an inverse trigonometric function is the classic case for u being the logarithm, since its derivative is algebraic.
The constant in v is free: adding K to v changes nothing, because the K terms cancel - OpenStax shows this explicitly.

example.prompt: Evaluate the integral from 0 to pi of x^2 cos x dx.
example.work: First round with u = x^2, dv = cos x dx, so du = 2x dx and v = sin x: the integral is [x^2 sin x] from 0 to pi minus the integral from 0 to pi of 2x sin x dx. The bracket is 0 at both ends. Second round on 2x sin x with u = 2x, dv = sin x dx, so du = 2 dx and v = -cos x: it equals [-2x cos x] from 0 to pi plus the integral from 0 to pi of 2 cos x dx, that is (2pi - 0) + 0 = 2pi. So the original integral is 0 - 2pi.

gateAngle: GATE CSE 2014 Set 3 Q.47 is this exact integral and its answer -2pi; GATE CSE 2025 Set 2 Q.2 needs one round of by parts on t ln t before the equation in x can be solved. The distractor pattern is the sign of the second bracket, so evaluate each bracket separately.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: GATE CSE 2014 Set 3 Q.47: the value of the integral from 0 to pi of x^2 cos x dx is (A) -2pi (B) pi (C) -pi (D) 2pi.
variations.why: Two rounds of by parts give [x^2 sin x + 2x cos x - 2 sin x] from 0 to pi. At pi the first and third terms vanish and 2x cos x is -2pi; at 0 the whole bracket is 0. The value is -6.2832, and the option -pi = -3.14 comes from dropping the factor 2.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: Evaluate the integral from 0 to 1 of x e^x dx.
variations.why: With u = x and dv = e^x dx, the integral is [x e^x] from 0 to 1 minus the integral from 0 to 1 of e^x dx = e - (e - 1) = 1. The value is exactly 1, which is worth remembering as the smallest self-checking by-parts example.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why does choosing u = cos x and dv = x^2 dx make the integral of x^2 cos x worse rather than better?
variations.answer: Because the new integral has a higher power of x in it.
variations.why: With that choice v = x^3/3, so the second integral carries x^3 sin x, a harder integrand than the one you started with. The rule of thumb is that u should get simpler when differentiated, which a polynomial always does and a cosine does not.

trap.what: Picking u so that the new integral is harder, or losing a sign when the second round produces a minus of a minus.
trap.why: By parts is a trade, not a solution: it helps only if the new integral is easier. And each round carries its own bracket, whose sign is easy to get wrong.
trap.counterexample: For the integral of x^2 cos x, taking u = cos x gives the new integral of (x^3/3) sin x, which is worse. And in the second round, [-2x cos x] from 0 to pi equals -2pi - 0 = -2pi only if the minus sign in v = -cos x is kept; dropping it gives +2pi and the wrong option (D).

check.question: Evaluate the integral from 1 to e of ln x dx.
check.explanation: With u = ln x, dv = dx, du = dx/x and v = x, the integral is [x ln x] from 1 to e minus the integral from 1 to e of 1 dx = (e - 0) - (e - 1) = 1. The logarithm must be u, because it is the only factor that becomes simpler when differentiated.
